chunks.section: SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE; TABLE OF CONTENTS.
chunks.content:
TITLE AND ENACTING CLAUSE
IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES A BILL To accelerate renewable
energy adoption while safeguarding economic vitality for small
businesses, rural agricultural producers, and vulnerable
wage-earning families. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of
Representatives of the United States of America in Congress
assembled,
SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE; TABLE OF CONTENTS.
(a) Short Title.·This Act may be cited as the 'Clean Energy
Transition and Small Business Economic Resilience Act of 2026'. (b)
Purpose.·The primary objective is to allocate federal grant
matching, reduce localized electricity tariffs, and provide targeted
micro-enterprise transition funds.

chunks.section: SECTION 2. FINDINGS AND DECLARATIONS OF IMPACT.
chunks.content:
SECTION 2. FINDINGS AND DECLARATIONS OF IMPACT.
(a) Small Business Vulnerability.·Commercial electricity rate
fluctuations disproportionately impact commercial enterprises
employing fewer than 50 individuals, particularly food service,
retail, and regional manufacturing. (b) Demographic
Disparities.·Rural low-income households allocate up to 14.2 percent
of disposable income to energy expenditures, representing a severe
energy burden that necessitates direct public assistance.

chunks.section: SECTION 3. MICRO-ENTERPRISE CLEAN ENERGY TRANSITION GRANTS.
chunks.content:
SECTION 3. MICRO-ENTERPRISE CLEAN ENERGY TRANSITION GRANTS.
(a) Establishment of Grant Facility.·The Secretary of Energy, in
consultation with the Small Business Administration, shall establish
the 'Commercial Decarbonization Incentive Program'. (b) Eligible
Entities.·An entity is eligible for a competitive grant under this
section if the entity: (1) Employs not more than 40 full-time
equivalent employees; (2) Maintains an average annual gross revenue
below $4,500,000 for the preceding 3 fiscal years; (3) Operates
primarily in designated rural or economically distressed municipal
corridors. (c) Grant Amounts.·Individual grants shall not exceed
$75,000 per commercial establishment, or 80 percent of qualified
capital costs for heat pump, solar photovoltaic, or commercial
battery storage installation. (d) Fast-Track
Disbursements.·Applications submitted by women-, veteran-, and
minority-owned small businesses shall receive priority review and

chunks.content:
battery storage installation. (d) Fast-Track
Disbursements.·Applications submitted by women-, veteran-, and
minority-owned small businesses shall receive priority review and
expedited determination within 21 business days of receipt.

chunks.section: SECTION 4. WORKFORCE RETRAINING AND DISPLACED WORKER STIPENDS.
chunks.content:
SECTION 4. WORKFORCE RETRAINING AND DISPLACED WORKER STIPENDS.
(a) Displaced Worker Wage Guarantee.·Eligible energy workers who
experience employment termination or reduction in hours due to
fossil-fuel thermal generation facility closures shall be entitled
to: (1) A transitional stipend of $2,400 per month for up to 18
consecutive months; (2) 100 percent tuition reimbursement for
certified technical apprenticeships or vocational certification at
community colleges; (3) Continuing healthcare coverage premium
subsidies under COBRA for a duration of 24 months. (b) Local Union
Apprenticeships.·Grants shall be awarded to accredited regional
labor organizations and community colleges to establish advanced
high-voltage line worker, wind turbine technician, and battery
storage technician training facilities. (c) Senior Worker
Protections.·Workers aged 55 and older shall be offered an expedited
bridge-to-pension option funded jointly through federal clean energy
transition reserves.

chunks.section: SECTION 5. MUNICIPAL INFRASTRUCTURE AND RESIDENTIAL UTILITY RELIEF.
chunks.content:
SECTION 5. MUNICIPAL INFRASTRUCTURE AND RESIDENTIAL UTILITY RELIEF.
(a) Low-Income Household Utility Bill Caps.·The Department of
Housing and Urban Development shall disburse direct block grants to
local utility providers to ensure that no residential customer with
an income below 200 percent of the federal poverty level is charged
more than 5 percent of gross household income for home heating and
electricity. (b) Rural Community Solar Co-Ops.·Allocates
$500,000,000 across fiscal years 2026 through 2029 for shared
agricultural community solar arrays. Farmers who dedicate
uncultivated land to community solar generation shall receive an
annual property tax credit of $1,200 per acre. (c) Public School
Weatherization.·Provides emergency funding for HVAC filtration and
insulation upgrades in public school districts where over 60 percent
of enrolled students qualify for the National School Lunch Program.

chunks.section: SECTION 6. COMPLIANCE, TRANSPARENCY, AND EFFECTIVE DATES.
chunks.content:
SECTION 6. COMPLIANCE, TRANSPARENCY, AND EFFECTIVE DATES.
(a) Reporting Requirements.·Not later than 180 days after the date
of enactment, the Comptroller General of the United States shall
submit to the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of
Representatives an initial audit regarding distribution equity. (b)
Anti-Gouging Provisions.·Retail electricity suppliers participating
in federal subsidy programs are strictly prohibited from raising
residential baseline kWh tariffs for a period of 36 months following
grant receipt. (c) Severability.·If any provision of this Act or its
application is held invalid, the remainder of the Act shall not be
affected. (d) Effective Date.·Except as otherwise explicitly
specified, this Act shall take effect on January 1, 2027.
